text:
sam: Thanks all — quick follow-up from today's all-hands re: customer wins and losses. I want this thread to be the canonical place for clarifying questions for leadership and any direct follow-ups. TL;DR: Recent wins were primarily about reliability, predictable latency (Dedicated), and transparent cost breakdowns. Losses skewed toward compliance gaps and a few feature gaps (SSO, per-route throttling). Please post short, concrete asks or customer quotes and tag relevant owners. We'll synthesize and publish a follow-up doc by EOW.

marta: Can we get a breakdown: wins by vertical (SaaS, fintech, healthcare)? even ballpark numbers help.

josh: From Sales — quick datapoint: 2 closes this quarter cited Dedicated latency SLA as a top reason; 1 enterprise lost because we couldn't commit to FedRAMP/HIPAA in their timeline. Top asks we're hearing: FedRAMP roadmap, SSO/SAML for Private, longer retention for logs.

li: Engineering note: FedRAMP is non-trivial — estimate ~6 months if we allocate a squad + infra. For SSO/SAML we can do a minimal MVP (SAML IdP + SCIM) in ~8 weeks with product priorities. Need leadership prioritization and a clear policy on compliance funding.

devon: Support: recurring customer feedback — they want per-route throttling and clearer quota alerts. Right now we get tickets asking "why tokens spiked" with no per-route context. If Product can surface per-route cost/latency in the console that would cut tickets. :point_up:

kelly: Growth — permission to publish a case study with Acme? They said yes on the call but I'd like a comms/ops signoff. Also, can we get a short one-pager on "why we won" for sales enablement?

marta: Adding a small ask — can Product/PLs list the top 3 roadmap asks from customers right now (SSO, FedRAMP, log retention) and indicate whether they're PR/paid features or free? Helps prioritize.

sam: Good asks. Quick answers: case study for Acme — yes, go ahead (please cc legal). We'll treat SSO as high priority for Private customers (target Q2 delivery for MVP). FedRAMP — leadership committed to scope & funding but realistically Q4 due to audit cycles. Log retention/per-route metrics — product should evaluate as medium priority; if we can tie to support cost savings we can accelerate.

josh: Noted. For customers asking FedRAMP, can we offer a short term workaround (dedicated contract language + network isolation) as a stopgap?

li: Potentially. We can offer network isolation + stricter SLAs, but we should be careful with compliance claims. Ops needs to document exact controls we provide.

ops-bot: New doc created: https://internal.redwood/docs/all-hands/wins-losses-followup (editable by @marta, @li, @josh).

devon: I pasted two direct customer quotes below from support tickets that might help the case study and PR: 
> "We switched to Redwood Dedicated because we finally hit consistent p95 under 120ms for our inference path."
> "We couldn't onboard until SAML was supported — had to choose another vendor."

kelly: I'll draft the sales one-pager and share in this thread for quick review.

marta: I'll populate the wins/losses doc with vertical breakdowns and the ask matrix (owner, ETA, paid/free). Expect a first pass by tomorrow AM.

sam: Thanks — leadership will review Marta's doc and come back with prioritization and any budget decisions. If anyone has more direct customer quotes or internal metrics (p95/p99 before vs after Dedicated), paste them here. Appreciate the short, focused replies. :raised_hands:
